title: cmux refactor switch
description: One refactor switch: plans/cmux-next/refactor-switches/<name>.json (plans/cmux-next/chrome-parity/p15-oracle.md, sections 3F.2 and 3I). A switch runs an old and a new arm of one refactor in one build, so the oracle can diff them (`oracle.py run --switch NAME --arm old|new`) and the new path can ship with a kill switch. It is the analog of a chrome/browser/flag-metadata.json entry (owners, expiry_milestone) plus its FlagExpectations file (expected_differences). scripts/cmux-next/oracle/switches.py --check runs this schema through normalize.py's validator, then the checks JSON Schema cannot express: expires <= created + 14 days, the app key is a RefactorSwitchKey raw value, the daemon key is in switches.rs SWITCH_NAMES, a config key is a settings row whose snapshot readback reads it, no app site reads the switch through a closure literal, and every expected_differences entry loads in diff.py.

name.description: The switch name: the file stem, the name a case lists in `switches` and `--switch` takes.

owner.description: Who deletes the old path before `expires` (a person, an agent role such as perf-lead, or an OWNERS.md owner).

plan.description: Repo-relative path of the plan that owns the refactor, with an optional #anchor. The file must exist.

read.description: launch: the arm is read once when the owner starts (the composition root or the daemon owner start) and passed as a plain value. live: sites ask the injected frozen value at each use. Either way the value never changes in a process, and no site reads it through a closure literal.

app_key.description: The app key: a raw value of `enum RefactorSwitchKey` in Packages/macOS/CmuxNext/Sources/CmuxNextCompat/RefactorSwitches.swift (p15-oracle-180), set with --cmux-switches=KEY=ARM or CMUX_NEXT_SWITCHES.

daemon_key.description: The daemon key: an entry of SWITCH_NAMES in cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui-core/src/switches.rs (p15-oracle-020), set with CMUX_TUI_SWITCHES=KEY=ARM.

config_key.description: A config arm: a dotted cmux-next.json settings key (a row `key` of schemas/settings/settings-schema.json) that the driver writes into the launch config, one value per arm (`config_arms`). For a virtual suite such as motion-on (p15-oracle-233): the same cases rerun with one setting changed, not a refactor's two code paths. It has no `expires`, its `planned` is its `default` (`oracle.py diff --arm launch-config` leaves it out; only `--switch NAME` runs its other arm), and the drivers apply it as a launch config value, never as a RefactorSwitches or CMUX_TUI_SWITCHES key.

config_arms.description: The config_key value of each arm; switches.py --check refuses two equal values and a value the settings row does not accept.

readback.description: JSON pointer into the snapshot where the product reads the applied config_key back (a snapshot-v1 value whose x-oracle-source `from` is config_key): each case's switch_readback.

default.description: The arm a process runs when nothing sets the switch.

planned.description: The arm the refactor lands at: `--arm launch-config` runs every switch at its planned arm against all-default.

created.description: The day the switch was registered (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC).

expires.description: The day the old path and this file must be gone: at most created + 14 days. `switches.py --expired` lists every switch whose day has come. Refactor switches (app_key, daemon_key) only: a config arm is a standing virtual suite, not a refactor, so it has no expiry and never enters the deletion queue.

suites.description: The minimum suites a both-arm run covers. Each is a suite of baselines.py SUITE_CLASSES.

expected_differences.description: Differences between the arms that are the point of the refactor: the FlagExpectations of this switch, read by diff.py --expected FILE. Empty when the arms must give equal snapshots.

old_paths.description: Repo-relative files or directories of the old arm, deleted with the switch. Each must exist while the switch does.

pointer.description: JSON pointer into the canonical snapshot; a difference at or under it is explained.

case.description: Case id glob (`suite/case`); default every case.

step.description: Step name glob; default every step.

task.description: The task that owns the difference.
